slides.title: Contradictory business details [create doubt].
slides.lede: One name on your website, another in a directory, an old office on a map. Each has an explanation. Together they weaken trust.

slides.title: What must match, and [what can adapt]

cards.label: Must match
cards.text: Public name, domain, phone, address, service areas, business category.

cards.label: Can adapt
cards.text: Length, emphasis, tone and examples used in each description.

slides.title: Five identities that [should not be interchangeable]

items.title: Parent organisation
items.text: Ownership, explained without replacing the brand.

items.title: Location
items.text: Accurate local address and phone details.

items.title: Product brand
items.text: Clearly separate or clearly part of it.

slides.title: Fix what customers see [at decision points] first
slides.text: A wrong legal name on a low-traffic directory may matter less than an inaccurate phone number on a prominent map listing. Prioritise by customer impact, not ease of editing.

slides.title: Consistency fails most often [during change]
slides.note: The brand changes quickly. **Third-party records do not.** Give change control the same status as financial control.

slides.quote: A consistent entity record does not guarantee visibility.
slides.text: It creates a dependable foundation on which visibility, reputation and brand equity can be built.
